newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No new Brazil B Band concessions seen before July.
newsitem.headline: No new Brazil B Band concessions seen before July.

text.p: Brazil is unlikely to grant further B Band cellular concessions until July because it will take several weeks to clear appeals filed by qualified and disqualified bidders, a Communications Ministry spokesman said.
"I see it as very unlikely that concessions will be granted by the end of this month. Maybe in July," said ministry spokesman Francisco Mendonca.
Mendonca said a total of 26 appeals were received by the late Wednesday deadline, including five from the consortia disqualified last week by the ministry's B Band privatization committee.
"Five were against the committee's decision to disqualify them. The others were qualified consortia attacking each other," he said.
The government has granted one B Band concession, but the administrative appeals must be cleared before further licenses can be granted, a process that could take weeks, he added.

The panel has five days to decide if it will reverse any disqualifications or pass the appeals on to Communications Minister Sergio Motta. Qualified groups have five days to respond to appeals before they go to the panel, which in turn has five days to decide what to do with the appeals, Mendonca said.
Moreover, if any group is unhappy with the ministry's decision, they may take their case to the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), he said.
The panel ruled five consortia ineligible -- Tess, Lightel, Algar, MCOM Wireless and Hutchinson-Cowan -- of 15 that presented bids in early April on nine of 10 concessions offered by the government.
Tess is comprised of telecom operator Telia of Sweden, Airline Cellular of Brazil, and Primave, part of Brazilian construction group C.R. Alameida.
Lightel is comprised of private telecoms operator Lightel, construction firm Queirroz Galvao, both of Brazil, and Korean Mobile Telecom.
Algar is the same group as Lightel, but has bid on separate areas.
MCOM Wireless is made up of the investment wing of Banco Garantia, Garantia Participacoes of Brazil, Telmex of Mexico, and U.S.-based Comcast.
Hutchison/Cowan is made up of telecoms group Hutchinson Whampoa of Hong Kong and Brazilian construction company Cowan Construtora.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Tuesday formally granted the first of the concessions, B Band area 7 covering central and western Brazil, to a Canadian-led group which made the only bid.
Americel SA bid of 338.5 million reais, 25.4 percent above the base price, for the license to operate cellular services in the area, which includes Brasilia.
The consortium is led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada and Telesystem, also of Canada, and also includes Citibank, local bank Opportunity and pension funds owned by Banco do Brasil.
